data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

# Task
Task: ajc-rr
Title: Bring the cluster-P Riemann-Roch substrate into AJC
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.rr,AJC.rr.principal

Give Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge the strongest honest Riemann-Roch and vanishing substrate available for the committed Picard representability route. Cluster P consists of the Euler-characteristic ledger, section-drop results, and uniform H1 vanishing needed downstream. AJC already contains a substantial sorry-free adelic lane, including RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiLedger.lean, but the sibling Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild contains a broader sorry-free 17,792-line RiemannRoch development. In particular, AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean proves a single-field bounded vanishing core; it does not by itself supply field-extension uniformity or global generation.

The owner of this task should decide, theorem by theorem, whether to reuse AJC code, port an AJCR result, adapt its argument, or rederive it in the AJC abstractions. Report that provenance honestly and do not promise a mechanical port. The one already identified open AJC leaf in this cone is principal-divisor degree zero in RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean. Work may close it when it materially advances the shared substrate.

This task owns only AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/** in AJC and may read AJCR without modifying it. It must not edit Picard/RigidPushforward files, Jacobian.lean, AbelJacobi.lean, the root import roll-up, or blueprint files. Notify ajc-gate when a vanishing or cohomology theorem becomes available so that gate hypotheses can be removed. Ask ajc-truth to add final root imports and to audit axioms of major landed results.

Done means the strongest reachable cluster-P statements are present under AJC-compatible hypotheses, focused Lean checks and the appropriate project build pass, no new anonymous or misleading sorry boundaries are introduced, #print axioms results are reported, and every remaining gap distinguishes single-field vanishing, extension-uniformity, and global generation precisely.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
148	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
281	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
282	  as **memory**.
283	
284	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
285	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
286	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
287	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
288	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
289	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
290	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
291	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
292	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
293	
294	## Resuming after an interruption
295	
296	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
298	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
299	
300	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
301	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
302	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
303	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
304	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
305	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
306	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
307	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
308	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
309	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
310	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
314	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
315	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
316	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
317	
318	## Final report (your last message)
319	
320	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
321	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
322	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
323	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
324	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
325	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
326	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
327	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
328	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
329	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
330	not by itself a reason to stop.
331	
332	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
333	
334	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
335	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
336	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
337	`subagents` skill):
338	
339	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
340	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
341	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
342	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
343	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
344	
345	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
346

2	name: horizon-start
3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
4	---
5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.
71	
72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
74	orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
75	stand before proposing work.
76	
77	One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
78	for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
79	`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
80	check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
81	resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
82	the run's original plan.)
83	
84	## Then, before you start
85	
86	- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
87	  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
88	- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
89	  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
90	  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
91	- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
92	  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
94	  `horizon-inbox`.
95	
96	Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
97	smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
98	here.
99

4

7	The provenance decision was **rederive adelically** throughout; nothing was ported, consistent with the standing finding that AJCR's substrate shares no identifiers with AJC. What I reused was an idea, and in adelic form it was far cheaper than in AJCR's sheaf form, because the injectivity half was already landed as node N14.

10	
11	- `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` (new, 810L, 0 sorry): the evaluation map `Γ(D)/Γ(D−P) → κ(P)`; injectivity unconditional, surjectivity from a **pair** of vanishings by rank–nullity. `GeneratedAt`, thresholds pointwise and uniform in `P`, plus the `residueDeg = 1` equivalence and its algebraically-closed derivation.

I called `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` a **discharge**; it isn't — its three stalk-level instance binders exist nowhere in AJC, and one I'd described as "the same finiteness node N14 consumes" is actually a separate gate. Separately, a hygiene pass showed my module had inherited an over-strong `∀ D` ledger binder, making a standing objection *wider*; three theorems now take it at only the two divisors they use — which is what makes the effective-cone result usable by the generation lane at all.

Gives `ell/h1dim/chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence` **unconditionally** — no gate, no finiteness, no ledger-exactness. AJCR's sheaf-level route needs the χ machinery even to *state* the transport. Plus the effective-witness dictionary.

Closed-ledger consequences take `hledger` as a named hypothesis, never a gate class.
11	- `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean` (new, 605L): single-field bounded H¹ vanishing with explicit `b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`; `exists_bound_ell_eq` upgrades ℓ from inequality to the formula `χ(0)+deg_k D`; `Peel.trans`/`of_list` reduce the peel input to a **one-point** bump with the list-effectivity side condition discharged, not assumed.

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — bounded `H¹` vanishing over a single base field
10	
11	This file assembles the **single-field bounded vanishing** statement of the
12	campaign's cluster P (P5, primary clause):
13	
14	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D))`
15	
16	from three inputs that are named explicitly in every statement:
17	
18	1. **a base vanishing** `Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`;
19	2. **the peel input** — surjectivity of the twist `Ȟ¹(D) ↠ Ȟ¹(D')` for `D ≤ D'`,
20	   in the concrete form `𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`.  This is exactly the `htwist`
21	   datum of the χ-ledger (`chi_add`), unwound;
22	3. **the closed ledger** `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, used only to produce an
23	   effective witness in the class of `D − D₀`.
24	
25	Inputs 1 and 2 are individually load-bearing, but they are **not** two independent
26	facts: `coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel` proves their conjunction equivalent to
27	vanishing on the whole cone `{D' ≥ D₀}`.  So the theorem's real content is
28	*cone-vanishing (pointwise condition) + ledger ⟹ degree-vanishing (numerical
29	condition)*, which is a genuine reduction — a divisor of large weighted degree need
30	not dominate `D₀` — but the input is a vanishing statement on an infinite family,
31	not one base vanishing plus a soft surjectivity.  The `_of_pointPeel` corollary is
32	the form that actually reduces the burden, to a one-point bump.
33	
34	Nothing here is a `sorry` and nothing here is a new gate class: each theorem is of
35	the form "given (1)–(3), the bound exists", with `b` computed explicitly as
36	`b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`.
37	
38	## Vanishing as `Subsingleton`, not as `h¹ = 0`
39	
40	Vanishing is stated as `Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)` rather than
41	`h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0`.  The two agree when `Ȟ¹(D)` is finite-dimensional, but the
42	`Subsingleton` form needs **no finiteness instance**, so §1 stays independent of the
43	finiteness gates.  `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts.
44	
45	**Do not over-read that.**  It is a claim about *instance arguments* in §1 only.
46	Every theorem taking the closed ledger `hledger` is a different matter: since
47	`Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space is `0`, an identity
48	`∀ D, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` silently forces finite-dimensionality wherever it
49	forces a nonzero rank.  So the ledger hypothesis carries finiteness content even
50	though no `Module.Finite` binder appears next to it.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` — `Ȟ¹(D) = 0 ⟺ 𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`: the concrete criterion
55	  everything below runs on.
56	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel` — the **peel step**: base vanishing at `D` plus the
57	  peel input transports vanishing to any `D' ≥ D`.
58	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_of_linearEquivalence` — vanishing is a class invariant
59	  (from `ClassInvariance.lean`, finiteness-free).
60	* `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` — the assembled bound.
61	
62	## Relation to the sibling project's `UniformVanishing.lean`
63	
64	`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` proves a statement of exactly this
65	shape, `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`, and its proof has the same
66	skeleton: fix a base twist, produce an effective witness of the residual class,
67	peel it, transport along the class.  **This file is not a port of it.**  AJCR's
68	version obtains its base vanishing from the FLV-class machine
69	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`, via a finite dominant `π : Y → ℙ¹` and the fiber
70	divisor) and its peel step from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`; neither the
71	FLV machinery nor `divisorSheaf` exists in AJC.  So here (1) and (2) are named
72	hypotheses rather than discharged lemmas, and the file is honest about that: what
73	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are
74	now proved.
75	
76	## The three gaps, kept apart
77	
78	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
79	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
80	things downstream consumers eventually want.  Of those two, the first is still open
81	anywhere in this project and the second is now proved elsewhere in the lane:
82	
83	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
84	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
85	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover
86	  (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` supplies `C_κ` as an AJC curve, but not the
87	  transported 2-affine cover data on which `Ȟ¹` here is pinned).
88	* **global generation** above the bound.  Needs `Ȟ¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed
89	  point `x`, i.e. the bound raised by the maximal residue degree, plus the
90	  evaluation-surjectivity argument.  **Now proved**, in
91	  `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`, from *this file's* three inputs and nothing more:
92	  the evaluation map is onto exactly when the section drop is maximal, which the
93	  ledger converts into the pair of vanishings at `D` and `D − x`
94	  (`evalMap_surjective`, `exists_bound_generatedAt`).  The uniform-over-points form
95	  additionally needs a bound on residue degrees, which is `1` over an algebraically
96	  closed base — and that residue fact is *reformulated* there
97	  (`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed`) onto stalk-level hypotheses that this project
98	  does not yet instantiate, so it is not discharged.  Read the warning in §7 of that
99	  file before citing it as one.
100	
101	`ajc-gate` should therefore not read this file as discharging an extension-uniform
102	hypothesis; it discharges the single-field bounded-vanishing shape only, and only
103	relative to (1)–(3).  For global generation, cite `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`,
104	which is conditional on the same (1)–(3).
105	-/

123	/-- **The concrete vanishing criterion.**  `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is trivial exactly
124	when the overlap sections are already coboundaries: `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`.  (The reverse
125	inclusion always holds, `coboundarySub_le_overlap`, so the condition really is
126	equality.) -/
127	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_iff (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
128	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) ↔
129	      sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D ≤ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := by
130	  constructor
131	  · intro hsub x hx
132	    have hzero : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
133	        (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
134	        (⟨x, hx⟩ : sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
135	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap,
136	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hzero
137	    exact hzero
138	  · intro hle
139	    constructor
140	    intro a b
141	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
142	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
143	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]
144	    exact hle ((sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).sub_mem x.2 y.2)
145	
146	/-- **The peel step.**  Suppose `Ȟ¹(D)` vanishes and the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')`
147	is surjective — concretely, every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees, modulo the
148	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
149	
150	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",
151	the step that turns one base vanishing into vanishing on a whole cone.  The
152	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
153	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
154	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
155	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
156	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
157	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
158	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
159	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
160	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
161	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
162	  intro x hx
163	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
164	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
165	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
166	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
167	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
168	  rw [this]
169	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB
170	
171	/-- **The peel relation `Peel D D'`.**  "Every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees,
172	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
173	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
174	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
175	than in one step. -/
176	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
177	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
178	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'

180	/-- **The peel relation is reflexive** (take `y = x`). -/
181	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
182	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
183	
184	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give

201	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel

482	
483	Both hypotheses of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` are individually load-bearing,
484	but that is **not** enough to call them two independent inputs, and the honest
485	description is sharper: their conjunction is *equivalent* to vanishing on the whole
486	cone above `D₀`.
487	
488	`ConeVanishing_iff_base_and_peel` below proves both directions.  `←` is
489	`subsingleton_h1Mod_peel`.  `→` is the direction that matters for honesty: given
490	cone-vanishing, `hpeel` holds by taking `y = 0`, since `x − 0 = x ∈ B(D')` is
491	exactly the vanishing criterion at `D'`.
492	
493	So `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` should be read as: **cone-vanishing above `D₀`
494	plus the ledger implies degree-vanishing above `b`.**  That is a genuine reduction
495	and not a re-indexing — the cone condition `D' ≥ D₀` is a *pointwise ordering*,
496	while the conclusion's condition `b ≤ deg_k D` is *numerical*, and a divisor of
497	large weighted degree need not dominate `D₀` at all.  Bridging the two is exactly
498	what the effective-witness/linear-equivalence transport does.  But it does mean the
499	input is a vanishing statement on an infinite family, not a single base vanishing
500	plus a soft surjectivity, and the `_of_pointPeel` corollary is the one that actually
501	reduces the burden (to a one-point bump).
502	
503	A second caveat, recorded for the same reason: `hledger` is not as
504	finiteness-innocent as it looks.  `Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space
505	is `0`, so an identity `∀ D, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` silently forces
506	finite-dimensionality wherever it forces a nonzero rank.  The claim that this file's
507	vanishing lane needs no finiteness instance is a statement about *instance
508	arguments* only; it does not apply to the theorems that take `hledger`. -/

510	/-- **`hbase ∧ hpeel` is exactly vanishing on the cone above `D₀`.**  See the
511	section note: `←` is `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel`, and `→` takes `y = 0`. -/
512	theorem coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) :
513	    (∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,

515	          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
516	        Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D')) ↔
517	      (Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀) ∧
518	        ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
519	          (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
520	            (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
521	          Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D') := by

523	  · intro hcone
524	    refine ⟨hcone D₀ (fun _ => le_rfl), fun D' hmono x hx => ?_⟩
525	    -- take `y = 0`: `x - 0 = x` is a coboundary by vanishing at `D'`

539	the shape that *can* be vacuous, and a reader is entitled to see that ruled out

541	does, since residue degrees are positive.) -/
542	theorem exists_degK_ge (b : ℤ) (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
543	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
544	    ∃ n : ℕ, b ≤ degK k ((n : ℤ) • pointDivisor P : X.WeilDivisor) := by
545	  refine ⟨b.toNat, ?_⟩
546	  rw [show degK k ((b.toNat : ℤ) • pointDivisor P : X.WeilDivisor)
547	        = (b.toNat : ℤ) • degK k (pointDivisor P : X.WeilDivisor) from
548	      map_zsmul (degKHom k) _ _, degK_pointDivisor, smul_eq_mul]
549	  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (residueDeg k P : ℤ) := by
550	    exact_mod_cast one_le_residueDeg k P
551	  have hb : b ≤ (b.toNat : ℤ) := Int.self_le_toNat b
552	  calc b ≤ (b.toNat : ℤ) := hb
553	    _ = (b.toNat : ℤ) * 1 := by ring
554	    _ ≤ (b.toNat : ℤ) * (residueDeg k P : ℤ) :=
555	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 (Int.natCast_nonneg _)
556	
557	/-- **The bound in numerical form.**  Same statement with the conclusion read on
558	`h¹` rather than on `Subsingleton`; `h1dim` is `0` for a subsingleton without any
559	finiteness input (`Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton`). -/
560	theorem exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero
561	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
562	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
563	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
564	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
565	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
566	      ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀,
567	        x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D') :
568	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 := by
569	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ :=
570	    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
571	  exact ⟨b, fun D hD => h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton k U₀ U₁ (hb D hD)⟩
572	
573	/-- **Above the bound, `ℓ` is computed exactly by the ledger:**
574	`ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`.  This is the Riemann–Roch conclusion in the vanishing
575	range — the shape a Grassmannian-embedding or rank-counting consumer wants, since
576	it turns `ℓ` from an inequality into a formula. -/
577	theorem ell_eq_of_bound
578	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
579	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hvan : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) :
580	    (ell k D : ℤ) = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D := by
581	  have hh1 := h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton k U₀ U₁ hvan
582	  have := hledger D
583	  rw [chi, hh1] at this
584	  omega
585	
586	/-- **Riemann–Roch in the vanishing range, assembled.**  Combining the bound with
587	`ell_eq_of_bound`: there is a threshold `b` past which `ℓ` is given by the *formula*
588	`ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, not merely bounded below by it.
589	
590	This is the single statement a downstream rank-counting consumer should quote: the
591	Riemann inequality `deg_k D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)` holds always
592	(`degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell`), and above `b` it is an equality.  With
593	`χ(0) = 1 − g` for the structure sheaf this is the classical
594	`ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g` for `deg` large.
595	
596	Conditional on the same three inputs as the bound, and single-field — see the
597	module docstring for why extension-uniformity and global generation are strictly
598	more. -/
599	theorem exists_bound_ell_eq
600	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
601	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
602	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
603	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
604	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
605	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D') :
606	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
607	      (ell k D : ℤ) = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D := by
608	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ :=
609	    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
610	  exact ⟨b, fun D hD => ell_eq_of_bound k U₀ U₁ hledger (hb D hD)⟩
611	
612	end Bound

9	/-!
10	# Adelic Riemann–Roch lane — Tier-0 substrate (nodes N1–N4)
11	
12	This file implements the Tier-0 substrate of the adelic Riemann–Roch lane
13	(design document §3, nodes N1–N4), built directly on top of the project's
14	`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.WeilDivisor` substrate (`PrimeDivisor`,
15	`RationalMap.order`, `IsRegularInCodimensionOne`, `WeilDivisor`).
16	
17	* **N2 `pointValuation`** — for a prime divisor `P` of a scheme `X` regular in
18	  codimension one, the DVR stalk `O_{X,P}` carries the height-one-spectrum adic
19	  valuation `v_P` on the function field `K(X)`; we identify the project's
20	  `Scheme.RationalMap.order P` with `-log ∘ v_P` (`order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation`).
21	* **N3 `sectionOfDivisor`** — the Riemann–Roch section subgroup
22	  `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f ∈ K(X) : ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }` as an
23	  `AddSubgroup K(X)`, together with the elementary order laws (monotonicity in
24	  `D`, the `min`/`⊔`-intersection identities, `1 ∈ L(0)`).
25	* **N1 `HasDedekindChart`** — the gate class packaging "every nonempty affine
26	  chart `Γ(X, U)` is a Dedekind domain" (design §4), with the Dedekind-from-DVR
27	  bridge `isDedekindDomain_of_forall_isLocalization_dvr`.
28	* **N4** — the affine-chart finiteness building block: on a Dedekind chart the
29	  set of height-one places at which a rational function is non-integral is finite
30	  (`IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite`).
31	
32	## The `RationalMap.order` ultrametric
33	
34	The one genuinely new analytic input is that `Scheme.RationalMap.order P` obeys
35	the ultrametric inequality `ord_P (f + g) ≥ min (ord_P f) (ord_P g)`, which makes
36	`sectionOfDivisor` closed under addition. It is derived from mathlib's
37	`Ring.ordFrac_eq_valuation_inv` (the DVR order-of-vanishing is the inverse of the
38	maximal-ideal adic valuation) plus `Valuation.map_add` and the monotonicity of
39	`WithZero.log` on nonzero elements.
40	
41	## References
42	
43	Design document `adelic-rr-lane-design.md` §§1–4; Stichtenoth,
44	*Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, ch. 1; Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*
45	II §6; Stacks 02RV, 02MD, 02IZ.
46	-/

58	/-! ## §N2. The point valuation of a prime divisor -/
59	
60	section PointValuation
61	
62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
63	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
64	
65	/-- **N2 — the point valuation `v_P`.** For a prime divisor `P` of a scheme `X`
66	that is regular in codimension one, the DVR stalk `O_{X,P.point}` has a maximal
67	ideal in its height-one spectrum, and the associated adic valuation of the
68	function field `K(X)` is the discrete valuation `v_P : K(X) → ℤᵐ⁰` at `P`. -/
69	noncomputable def pointValuation (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
70	    Valuation X.functionField ℤᵐ⁰ :=
71	  (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)).valuation
72	    X.functionField
73	
74	/-- **N2 identification.** The project's `Scheme.RationalMap.order P` equals
75	`-log ∘ v_P`, i.e. the additive normalisation of the point valuation `v_P`. This
76	is the bridge between the `Ring.ordFrac`-based `order` and mathlib's
77	height-one-spectrum adic valuation. -/
78	theorem order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
79	    (f : X.functionField) :
80	    Scheme.RationalMap.order P f = -(WithZero.log (pointValuation P f)) := by
81	  unfold Scheme.RationalMap.order pointValuation
82	  rw [Ring.ordFrac_eq_valuation_inv, WithZero.log_inv]
83	
84	/-- **The `order` ultrametric.** For nonzero `f, g` with `f + g ≠ 0`, the order of
85	the sum is at least the minimum of the orders. This is the valuation-theoretic
86	triangle inequality `v_P(f + g) ≥ min (v_P f) (v_P g)` for the additive
87	normalisation `ord_P = -log ∘ v_P`; it is what makes `sectionOfDivisor` closed
88	under addition. -/
89	theorem order_add_ge_min (P : X.PrimeDivisor) {f g : X.functionField}
90	    (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) (hfg : f + g ≠ 0) :
91	    min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) ≤
92	      Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := by
93	  simp only [order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation]
94	  set v := pointValuation P with hv
95	  have hvf : v f ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hf
96	  have hvg : v g ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hg
97	  have hvfg : v (f + g) ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hfg
98	  have hadd : v (f + g) ≤ max (v f) (v g) := v.map_add f g
99	  rcases le_total (v f) (v g) with h | h
100	  · have hle : v (f + g) ≤ v g := hadd.trans (by rw [max_eq_right h])
101	    have hlog : WithZero.log (v (f + g)) ≤ WithZero.log (v g) :=
102	      (WithZero.log_le_log hvfg hvg).mpr hle
103	    calc min (-(WithZero.log (v f))) (-(WithZero.log (v g)))
104	        ≤ -(WithZero.log (v g)) := min_le_right _ _
105	      _ ≤ -(WithZero.log (v (f + g))) := by linarith
106	  · have hle : v (f + g) ≤ v f := hadd.trans (by rw [max_eq_left h])
107	    have hlog : WithZero.log (v (f + g)) ≤ WithZero.log (v f) :=
108	      (WithZero.log_le_log hvfg hvf).mpr hle
109	    calc min (-(WithZero.log (v f))) (-(WithZero.log (v g)))
110	        ≤ -(WithZero.log (v f)) := min_le_left _ _
111	      _ ≤ -(WithZero.log (v (f + g))) := by linarith
112	
113	end PointValuation

115	/-! ## §N3. Riemann–Roch section subgroups `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))` -/
116	
117	section Sections
118	
119	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
120	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
121	
122	/-- **N3 — the Riemann–Roch section subgroup `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`.** For an open
123	`U ⊆ X` and a Weil divisor `D`, the set of rational functions `f ∈ K(X)` whose
124	order along every prime divisor `P` meeting `U` is at least `-D(P)`:
125	`Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f : f = 0 ∨ ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }`.
126	
127	The `f = 0` disjunct encodes the convention `ord_P 0 = +∞` (the project's junk
128	convention gives `ord_P 0 = 0`, so the zero function must be admitted separately).
129	Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric `order_add_ge_min`. -/
130	def sectionOfDivisor (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
131	    AddSubgroup X.functionField where
132	  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
133	    -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }
134	  zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
135	  add_mem' := by
136	    intro f g hf hg
137	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
138	    · simpa using hg
139	    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hgne
140	    · simpa using hf
141	    rcases eq_or_ne (f + g) 0 with h0 | h0
142	    · exact Or.inl h0
143	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
144	    have hcf := (hf.resolve_left hfne) P hP
145	    have hcg := (hg.resolve_left hgne) P hP
146	    calc -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
147	        ≤ min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) :=
148	          le_min hcf hcg
149	      _ ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := order_add_ge_min P hfne hgne h0
150	  neg_mem' := by
151	    intro f hf
152	    rcases hf with rfl | hf
153	    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
154	    · refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
155	      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_neg]
156	      exact hf P hP
157	
158	/-- Membership in `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`. -/
159	theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
160	    {f : X.functionField} :
161	    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
162	      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f :=
163	  Iff.rfl
164	
165	/-- Membership for a nonzero function: only the order condition remains. -/
166	theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
168	    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
169	      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f := by
170	  rw [mem_sectionOfDivisor, or_iff_right hf]
171	
172	/-- **Monotonicity in the divisor.** If `D ≤ D'` pointwise then
173	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ⊆ Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`. -/
174	theorem sectionOfDivisor_mono (U : X.Opens) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
175	    (h : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
176	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
177	    sectionOfDivisor U D ≤ sectionOfDivisor U D' := by
178	  intro f hf
179	  rcases hf with rfl | hf
180	  · exact Or.inl rfl
181	  exact Or.inr fun P hP => (neg_le_neg (h P)).trans (hf P hP)
182	
183	/-- **`1 ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪(0))`** — the seed of `L(0) ⊇ k`. -/
184	theorem one_mem_sectionOfDivisor_zero (U : X.Opens) :
185	    (1 : X.functionField) ∈ sectionOfDivisor U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) := by
186	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
187	  rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]
188	  change -((0 : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ) P) ≤ 0
189	  simp
190	
191	/-- **Intersection over opens.** A section over `U₁ ⊔ U₂` is exactly a section
192	over `U₁` intersected with a section over `U₂`. -/
193	theorem sectionOfDivisor_sup (U₁ U₂ : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
194	    sectionOfDivisor (U₁ ⊔ U₂) D =
195	      sectionOfDivisor U₁ D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U₂ D := by
196	  ext f
197	  rw [AddSubgroup.mem_inf, mem_sectionOfDivisor, mem_sectionOfDivisor,
198	    mem_sectionOfDivisor]
199	  constructor
200	  · rintro (rfl | h)
201	    · exact ⟨Or.inl rfl, Or.inl rfl⟩
202	    · exact ⟨Or.inr fun P hP => h P (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup.mpr (Or.inl hP)),
203	        Or.inr fun P hP => h P (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup.mpr (Or.inr hP))⟩
204	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
205	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
206	    · exact Or.inl rfl
207	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
208	    rcases (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup).mp hP with hP1 | hP2
209	    · exact (h1.resolve_left hfne) P hP1
210	    · exact (h2.resolve_left hfne) P hP2
211	
212	/-- **Intersection of divisor conditions is the `min` divisor.** If `E` is the
213	pointwise minimum of `D` and `D'`, then `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) = Γ(U, 𝒪(E))`,
214	i.e. `L(D) ∩ L(D') = L(min D D')`. -/
215	theorem sectionOfDivisor_inf_divisor (U : X.Opens) {D D' E : X.WeilDivisor}
216	    (hE : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P =
217	      min ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
218	        ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)) :
219	    sectionOfDivisor U D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U D' = sectionOfDivisor U E := by
220	  ext f
221	  rw [AddSubgroup.mem_inf, mem_sectionOfDivisor, mem_sectionOfDivisor,
222	    mem_sectionOfDivisor]
223	  constructor
224	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
225	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
226	    · exact Or.inl rfl
227	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
228	    rw [hE P]
229	    rcases le_total ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
230	        ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) with hle | hle
231	    · rw [min_eq_left hle]; exact (h1.resolve_left hfne) P hP
232	    · rw [min_eq_right hle]; exact (h2.resolve_left hfne) P hP
233	  · rintro (rfl | h)
234	    · exact ⟨Or.inl rfl, Or.inl rfl⟩
235	    · exact ⟨Or.inr fun P hP =>
236	          ((by rw [hE P]; exact neg_le_neg (min_le_left _ _)) :
237	            _ ≤ -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P)).trans (h P hP),
238	        Or.inr fun P hP =>
239	          ((by rw [hE P]; exact neg_le_neg (min_le_right _ _)) :
240	            _ ≤ -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P)).trans (h P hP)⟩
241	
242	/-- **The Riemann–Roch space `L(D)`.** Global sections of `𝒪_X(D)`: the section
243	over all of `X`. On a 2-affine cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` this is
244	`Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D))`, the kernel of the Čech difference map. -/
245	def linearSystem (D : X.WeilDivisor) : AddSubgroup X.functionField :=
246	  sectionOfDivisor ⊤ D
247	
248	/-- On a 2-affine cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, `L(D)` is the intersection of the two
249	chart sections. -/
250	theorem linearSystem_eq_inf {U₀ U₁ : X.Opens} (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
251	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
252	    linearSystem D = sectionOfDivisor U₀ D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U₁ D := by
253	  rw [linearSystem, ← hcov, sectionOfDivisor_sup]
254	
255	end Sections
256	
257	/-! ## §N1. Dedekind coordinate rings of affine charts -/
258	
259	section Chart
260	
261	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
262	
263	/-- **N1 (unconditional half) — the affine chart is a fraction-ring chart.** For a
264	nonempty affine open `U` of an integral scheme, the coordinate ring `Γ(X, U)` has
265	`K(X)` as its fraction field. Thin wrapper around mathlib's
266	`functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen`. -/
267	theorem chartRing_isFractionRing [IsIntegral X] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
268	    [Nonempty U] : IsFractionRing Γ(X, U) X.functionField :=
269	  functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen X U hU
270	
271	/-- **N1 (unconditional half) — the affine chart is Noetherian.** For a nonempty
272	affine open `U` of a locally Noetherian scheme, `Γ(X, U)` is a Noetherian ring. -/
273	theorem chartRing_isNoetherianRing [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {U : X.Opens}
274	    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U) :=
275	  IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian ⟨U, hU⟩
276	
277	/-- **N1 — the Dedekind-from-DVR bridge** (pure ring theory, `IsDedekindDomainDvr`).
278	A Noetherian integral domain whose localization at every nonzero prime is a
279	discrete valuation ring is a Dedekind domain. This is exactly the criterion under
280	which a smooth (equivalently: regular, on a curve) affine chart `Γ(X, U)` is
281	Dedekind; the missing input is that every nonzero prime of the chart is
282	height-one, i.e. that `X` is a curve. -/
283	theorem isDedekindDomain_of_forall_localization_dvr {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
284	    [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
285	    (h : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ →
286	      IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime P)) :
287	    IsDedekindDomain R := by
288	  haveI : IsDedekindDomainDvr R := by
289	    refine { is_dvr_at_nonzero_prime := fun P hP hPp => ?_ }
290	    haveI := hPp
291	    exact h P hP
292	  infer_instance
293	
294	/-- **N1 (gate) — `HasDedekindChart`.** Packages "every nonempty affine chart of
295	`X` has a Dedekind coordinate ring". On a smooth (or normal) curve this holds
296	because each chart is a one-dimensional regular Noetherian domain; where mathlib's
297	`smooth ⇒ regular chart` bridge is unavailable we supply this as a `HasPicScheme`-
298	style gate class (no global instance — an honest hypothesis), to be discharged
299	later via `isDedekindDomain_of_forall_localization_dvr` (design §4). -/
300	class HasDedekindChart (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] : Prop where
301	  /-- Every nonempty affine chart is a Dedekind domain. -/
302	  isDedekindDomain : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → [Nonempty U] →
303	    IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, U)
304

306	theorem isDedekindDomain_chart [IsIntegral X] [HasDedekindChart X] {U : X.Opens}

312	/-! ## §N4. Finiteness of the places of a rational function on a chart
313	
314	The scheme-level statement `rationalMap_order_finite_support` in
315	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean` (that `P ↦ ord_P f` has finite support) is **false**
316	as pinned there with only `[IsLocallyNoetherian X]`: the "line with infinitely many
317	origins" is integral, locally Noetherian and regular in codimension one, yet `t`
318	has order one at each of its infinitely many origins.  Finiteness needs `X`
319	globally Noetherian (`[IsNoetherian X]`, i.e. quasi-compact), matching Stacks 02RV.
320	
321	What *is* unconditionally true, and is the reusable core of the affine-chart
322	argument, is the following: on a single Dedekind chart, a nonzero rational function
323	is non-integral (valuation `≠ 1`) at only finitely many height-one places. -/

331	Dedekind domain `R`, only finitely many height-one places `v` have `v(k) ≠ 1`
332	(i.e. only finitely many places where `k` is a zero or a pole). This is the
333	finite-support statement for the principal divisor on a single affine chart,
334	obtained from mathlib's `HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite` applied to `k` and to
335	`k⁻¹`. -/
336	theorem finite_places_ne_one {k : K} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
337	    {v : HeightOneSpectrum R | v.valuation K k ≠ 1}.Finite := by
338	  have h1 := HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite R k
339	  have h2 := HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite R k⁻¹
340	  refine (h1.union h2).subset fun v hv => ?_
341	  simp only [HeightOneSpectrum.Support, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hv ⊢
342	  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hv with hlt | hgt
343	  · right
344	    rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, map_inv₀]
345	    have hv0 : v.valuation K k ≠ 0 := by
346	      simpa using (Valuation.zero_iff (v.valuation K)).not.mpr hk
347	    exact one_lt_inv₀ (lt_of_le_of_ne zero_le (Ne.symm hv0)) |>.mpr hlt
348	  · exact Or.inl hgt
349

1352	
1353	/-- **Linear equivalence of Weil divisors.**
1354	
1355	Two Weil divisors `D, D' ∈ Div(X)` are linearly equivalent, written `D ~ D'`, if
1356	and only if there exists a nonzero rational function `f ∈ K(X)^×` with
1357	`D - D' = div(f) ∈ Div(X)`.
1358	
1359	`~` is an equivalence relation (reflexivity from `div(1) = 0`, symmetry from
1360	`div(f⁻¹) = -div(f)`, transitivity from `div(fg) = div(f) + div(g)`, all via
1361	`thm:principal_hom`). The quotient `Cl(X) := Div(X) / im(div)` is the
1362	**divisor class group** of `X`.
1363	
1364	On a smooth proper curve `C` over `k̄`, `thm:principal_deg_zero` shows the
1365	degree map descends to `deg : Cl(C) → ℤ`.
1366	
1367	Blueprint reference: `def:linear_equivalence` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 131). -/
1368	def LinearEquivalence [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
1369	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
1370	  ∃ (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0), D - D' = principal f hf

9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the residue-weighted degree and the section-drop bounds
10	
11	This file supplies two further legs of the campaign's cluster P
12	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, P3/P4):
13	
14	* the **residue-weighted (adelic) degree** `deg_k D = Σ_P D(P)·[κ(P):k]`, which is
15	  the degree the χ-ledger actually telescopes to (the geometric
16	  `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` is its specialisation at residue degree one, i.e.
17	  over an algebraically closed base field);
18	* the **section-drop bounds** `ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(D + P) ≤ ℓ(D) + [κ(P):k]`;
19	* **residue-degree positivity** `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]` and its consequence that a nonzero
20	  effective divisor has *positive* weighted degree.
21	
22	The drop bounds are **unconditional** — they need neither the ledger's
23	connecting/surjectivity data nor the strong-approximation input, only the
24	finite-dimensionality instances.  The `≤` direction of the one-point step is
25	`localStep_finrank_le` (node N14, already landed) read through the rank–nullity
26	identity `finrank_localStepDom`; that is precisely the observation that the
27	*upper* bound of the χ-ledger does not need the residue map to be onto.
28	
29	## Statements whose ledger input is explicit
30	
31	The results that genuinely need the closed ledger `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` take it
32	as an explicit hypothesis `hledger`, in the same style as the existing
33	`Adelic.riemann_inequality`.  Nothing here introduces a new gate class, and no
34	statement is left as a `sorry`.  Under that hypothesis this file derives:
35	
36	* `degK_principal_eq_zero` — **principal divisors have residue-weighted degree
37	  zero**, from the class-invariance of `χ` (`ClassInvariance.lean`).  This is the
38	  adelic form of the open geometric leaf
39	  `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`.
40	* `degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one` and
41	  `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` — the collapse to the
42	  **unweighted** degree when every residue degree is one, and the resulting
43	  unweighted principal-degree-zero statement.  Together these reduce the open leaf
44	  to the single residue-field fact `[κ(P):k̄] = 1` plus instance plumbing; §4
45	  records why the `sorry` is nonetheless left in place.
46	* `ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg` — `deg_k D < 0 ⟹ ℓ(D) = 0` (campaign P4(a)).
47	* `degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` — the Riemann inequality in closed weighted form.
48	
49	## What is NOT proved here (read this before consuming)
50	
51	Three distinct gaps in the vanishing story are kept apart deliberately:
52	
53	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → h¹(D) = 0`, for
54	   one fixed base field `k`.  Not proved here and not derivable from the ledger
55	   alone: it needs a base vanishing `h¹(𝒪(n₀·x₀)) = 0` plus surjectivity of
56	   `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` (the "peel an effective divisor" step).  The sibling project
57	   proves its analogue (`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean`) from an
58	   FLV-class machine that has no AJC counterpart.
59	2. **Extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
60	   Strictly more than (1): it needs flat base change of the bound along
61	   `k → κ`.  Nothing in this file quantifies over extensions.
62	3. **Global generation** — `𝒪(D)` generated by global sections above the bound.
63	   Strictly more than (1): it needs `h¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed point, i.e. the
64	   bound raised by the maximum residue degree.  Not addressed *in this file*, but
65	   proved in `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` from the same inputs as (1); it is the
66	   equality case of this file's own drop bound `ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg`.  It is
67	   **not** more than (2): global generation and extension uniformity are independent,
68	   and (2) remains open.

71	
72	The residue-weighted degree, the drop bound and the `deg < 0 ⟹ ℓ = 0` corollary
73	are **rederived in the AJC adelic abstractions**; they are not ports.  The
74	sibling `AJCR RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean` / `Degree.lean` prove related
75	statements on the `CurveDivisor`/`divisorSheaf` substrate, whose names do not
76	exist in this project.  The argument reused from AJCR is the χ-transport step of
77	`deg_divOf`; its AJC counterpart is `chi_eq_of_principal_shift`.
78	-/

90	/-! ## §1. The residue-weighted (adelic) degree -/
91	
92	section DegK
93	
94	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
95	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
96	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
97	
98	/-- **The residue-weighted degree homomorphism `deg_k : Div(X) →+ ℤ`.**
99	`deg_k D = Σ_P D(P)·[κ(P):k]`, the degree the χ-ledger telescopes to
100	(`chi_telescope_list`).  Bundled as an `AddMonoidHom` through
101	`Finsupp.liftAddHom`, exactly as the unweighted `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree_hom`
102	is, so additivity, `deg_k 0 = 0` and `deg_k (-D) = -deg_k D` come for free.
103	
104	Over an algebraically closed base field every closed point of a smooth curve has
105	`[κ(P):k] = 1` and this is the geometric degree; over a general `k` the weighting
106	is what makes the degree a linear-equivalence invariant. -/
107	noncomputable def degKHom : X.WeilDivisor →+ ℤ :=
108	  Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun P : X.PrimeDivisor =>
109	    (AddMonoidHom.mulRight ((residueDeg k P : ℤ)) : ℤ →+ ℤ))
110	
111	/-- **The residue-weighted degree of a Weil divisor.** -/
112	noncomputable def degK (D : X.WeilDivisor) : ℤ := degKHom k D
113	
114	theorem degK_eq_sum (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
115	    degK k D = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D).sum
116	      (fun P n => n * (residueDeg k P : ℤ)) :=
117	  Finsupp.liftAddHom_apply (α := X.PrimeDivisor) (M := ℤ) (N := ℤ) _ _
118	
119	@[simp] theorem degK_zero : degK k (0 : X.WeilDivisor) = 0 := map_zero _
120	
121	theorem degK_add (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) :
122	    degK k (D + D') = degK k D + degK k D' := map_add _ _ _
123	
124	@[simp] theorem degK_neg (D : X.WeilDivisor) : degK k (-D) = -degK k D :=
125	  map_neg _ _
126	
127	theorem degK_sub (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) :
128	    degK k (D - D') = degK k D - degK k D' := map_sub _ _ _
129	
130	/-- **The one-point divisor has weighted degree the residue degree.** -/
131	@[simp] theorem degK_pointDivisor (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
132	    degK k (pointDivisor P : X.WeilDivisor) = (residueDeg k P : ℤ) := by
133	  rw [degK_eq_sum, pointDivisor]
134	  exact (Finsupp.sum_single_index (by simp)).trans (one_mul _)
135	
136	/-- **The weighted degree of a list-effective divisor is the sum of the residue
137	degrees** — the numerical companion of `chi_telescope_list`. -/
138	theorem degK_divisorOfList (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
139	    degK k (divisorOfList L : X.WeilDivisor) = ((L.map (residueDeg k)).sum : ℤ) := by
140	  induction L with
141	  | nil => simp [divisorOfList]
142	  | cons P L ih =>
143	    rw [divisorOfList, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor, ih, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
144	    push_cast
145	    ring
146	
147	/-- **An effective divisor has nonnegative weighted degree.**  Each summand
148	`D(P)·[κ(P):k]` is a product of nonnegative integers. -/
149	theorem degK_nonneg_of_nonneg {D : X.WeilDivisor}
150	    (hD : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, 0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) :
151	    0 ≤ degK k D := by
152	  rw [degK_eq_sum, Finsupp.sum]
153	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun P _ =>
154	    mul_nonneg (hD P) (Int.natCast_nonneg _)
155	
156	/-- **The residue field is nontrivial**: `1 ∈ orderGe P 0` but `1 ∉ orderGe P 1`,
157	since `ord_P 1 = 0`.  So the one-step valuation quotient
158	`localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` — the residue field `κ(P)` — is
159	not the zero space. -/
160	theorem nontrivial_localStepTgt_one (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
161	    Nontrivial (localStepTgt k P 1) := by
162	  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
163	    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
164	    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
165	  refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨1, hone⟩, 0, ?_⟩
166	  intro h
167	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
168	    mem_orderGeSub] at h
169	  rcases h with h0 | h0
170	  · exact one_ne_zero h0
171	  · rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one] at h0
172	    norm_num at h0
173	
174	/-- **The residue degree is positive**: `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]`.  From the nontriviality of
175	`κ(P)` (`nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`) plus finite-dimensionality — a nontrivial
176	finite-dimensional space has positive rank.  Needed wherever a *nonzero* effective
177	divisor must be given *positive* degree. -/
178	theorem one_le_residueDeg (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
179	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] : 1 ≤ residueDeg k P := by
180	  haveI := nontrivial_localStepTgt_one k P
181	  rw [residueDeg, Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
182	  intro h
183	  exact (not_subsingleton (localStepTgt k P 1))
184	    ((Module.finrank_zero_iff (R := k)).mp h)
185	
186	/-- **A nonzero effective divisor has positive weighted degree.**  Some coefficient
187	`D(P₀)` is `≥ 1` (it is nonzero and `≥ 0`) and contributes `D(P₀)·[κ(P₀):k] ≥ 1`
188	by `one_le_residueDeg`, while every other summand is `≥ 0`.
189	
190	This is the adelic counterpart of the sibling project's
191	`CurveDivisor.deg_pos_of_nonneg_of_ne_zero`; the argument is the standard one, but
192	the residue-degree positivity input (`one_le_residueDeg`) is proved here from the
193	project's own `orderGe` filtration rather than from a residue-field API. -/
194	theorem degK_pos_of_nonneg_of_ne_zero {D : X.WeilDivisor}
195	    (hD : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, 0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
196	    (hne : D ≠ 0)
197	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
198	    0 < degK k D := by
199	  classical
200	  -- some coefficient is nonzero, hence ≥ 1
201	  obtain ⟨P₀, hP₀⟩ : ∃ P₀ : X.PrimeDivisor,
202	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P₀ ≠ 0 := by
203	    by_contra hno
204	    push Not at hno
205	    exact hne (Finsupp.ext hno)
206	  have hP₀supp : P₀ ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D).support :=
207	    Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hP₀
208	  rw [degK_eq_sum, Finsupp.sum, ← Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ hP₀supp]
209	  have hrest : 0 ≤ ∑ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D).support.erase P₀,
210	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P * (residueDeg k P : ℤ) :=
211	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun P _ => mul_nonneg (hD P) (Int.natCast_nonneg _)
212	  have hlast : 0 < (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P₀ * (residueDeg k P₀ : ℤ) := by
213	    have h1 : 1 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P₀ := by
214	      have := hD P₀; omega
215	    have h2 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (residueDeg k P₀ : ℤ) := by
216	      exact_mod_cast one_le_residueDeg k P₀
217	    calc (0 : ℤ) < 1 * 1 := by norm_num
218	      _ ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P₀ * (residueDeg k P₀ : ℤ) :=
219	          mul_le_mul h1 h2 (by norm_num) (by linarith)
220	  linarith
221	
222	/-- **The weighted degree agrees with the geometric degree when every residue
223	degree is one.**  `deg_k D = Σ_P D(P)·[κ(P):k]` collapses to
224	`Σ_P D(P) = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D` as soon as `[κ(P):k] = 1` at every prime
225	divisor in the support — which is the case over an algebraically closed base
226	field, every closed point of a smooth curve then having residue field `k` itself.
227	
228	This is the **only** thing separating the adelic `degK_principal_eq_zero` from the
229	geometric leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`; see §4.  The hypothesis
230	is stated pointwise on the support rather than globally so that a caller can
231	discharge it where it is actually needed. -/
232	theorem degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one {D : X.WeilDivisor}
233	    (h1 : ∀ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D).support, residueDeg k P = 1) :
234	    degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D := by
235	  rw [degK_eq_sum, Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree, Finsupp.sum, Finsupp.sum]
236	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun P hP => ?_
237	  rw [h1 P hP]
238	  simp
239	
240	end DegK
