242	/-! ## §2. The section-drop bounds (unconditional)
243	
244	For a one-point twist `D' = D + P` the local step space
245	`Γ(⊤,𝒪(D'))/Γ(⊤,𝒪(D))` has dimension `ℓ(D') − ℓ(D)` (rank–nullity,
246	`finrank_localStepDom`) and dimension at most `[κ(P):k]` (node N14,
247	`localStep_finrank_le` applied at `U = ⊤`).  Both facts are already in the
248	project; combining them gives the classical section-drop sandwich
249	`ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(D + P) ≤ ℓ(D) + [κ(P):k]` with **no** ledger exactness hypothesis and
250	**no** strong-approximation input — those are needed only for the `h¹` half of the
251	ledger, not for the `ℓ` half. -/
252	
253	section Drops
254	
255	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
256	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
257	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
258	
259	/-- **`ℓ` is monotone in the divisor.**  `D ≤ D'` pointwise gives
260	`Γ(⊤,𝒪(D)) ⊆ Γ(⊤,𝒪(D'))`, hence `ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(D')`. -/
261	theorem ell_mono {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
262	    (hDD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
263	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)
264	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D')] :
265	    ell k D ≤ ell k D' :=
266	  Submodule.finrank_mono (sectionSub_mono k ⊤ hDD')
267	
268	/-- **The one-point section-drop bound (unconditional).**  For a one-point twist
269	`D' = D + P`,
270	`ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(D') ≤ ℓ(D) + [κ(P):k]`.
271	
272	The upper bound is node N14 (`localStep_finrank_le` at `U = ⊤`) read through
273	rank–nullity (`finrank_localStepDom`); the lower bound is `ell_mono`.  Neither
274	half consumes the ledger's connecting/surjectivity data. -/
275	theorem ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
276	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
277	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
278	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
279	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
280	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
281	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
282	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D')]
283	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
284	    ell k D ≤ ell k D' ∧ (ell k D' : ℤ) ≤ ell k D + residueDeg k P := by
285	  refine ⟨ell_mono k hle, ?_⟩
286	  have hrn := finrank_localStepDom k ⊤ (sectionSub_mono k ⊤ hle)
287	  have hN14 := localStep_finrank_le k (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_top P.point)
288	    hstep hle hoff
289	  have hcast : (Module.finrank k (localStepDom k ⊤ D D') : ℤ) ≤ (residueDeg k P : ℤ) := by
290	    exact_mod_cast hN14
291	  simp only [ell] at *
292	  omega
293	
294	/-- **The one-point drop bound in `pointDivisor` spelling.**  For the concrete
295	twist `D' = 1·P + D` the three coordinate hypotheses of
296	`ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg` are discharged by the `pointDivisor` calculus of the
297	χ-ledger, leaving the clean statement
298	`ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(P + D) ≤ ℓ(D) + [κ(P):k]`. -/
299	theorem ell_add_pointDivisor_le (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
300	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ (pointDivisor P + D))]
301	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
302	    ell k D ≤ ell k (pointDivisor P + D) ∧
303	      (ell k (pointDivisor P + D) : ℤ) ≤ ell k D + residueDeg k P :=
304	  ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg k (add_pointDivisor_apply_self D P)
305	    (le_add_pointDivisor D P)
306	    (fun _ hQ => (add_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne D hQ).symm)
307	
308	end Drops

310	/-! ## §3. Consequences of the closed ledger
311	
312	The **closed ledger** is the identity `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for every Weil
313	divisor `D`.  In this project it is not a theorem: `chi_telescope_list` proves it
314	for *effective* divisors from a per-step hypothesis which is one application of
315	`chi_add_eq_residueDeg`, and that in turn consumes the ledger's
316	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input `hsurj`.  So the
317	statements below take the closed ledger as an explicit hypothesis, spelled
318	exactly as it will be discharged:
319	
320	`hledger : ∀ D, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D`.
321	
322	That is an honest hypothesis, not a gate class and not a `sorry`: each theorem
323	here says "given the ledger, this follows", and the reader can see what is
324	missing. -/
325	
326	section Ledger
327	
328	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
329	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
330	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
331	
332	/-- **The ledger holds on list-effective divisors, given the one-point bump.**
333	`chi_telescope_list` computes `χ(Σ_{P ∈ L} P)` as `χ(0) + Σ_{P ∈ L} deg P`, and
334	`degK_divisorOfList` computes `deg_k` of the same divisor as the same sum, so the
335	two agree: `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for `D = divisorOfList L`.
336	
337	This is what pins `degK` as *the* degree of the ledger rather than one weighting
338	among several, and it shows the `hledger` hypothesis of this section is not
339	idle — it holds wherever the one-point bump `hbump` does, which is one application
340	of `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` per step.  What `hbump` still costs is the ledger's
341	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input, and extending
342	from list-effective divisors to *all* divisors additionally needs the negative
343	part; both are why the general ledger is a hypothesis and not a theorem here. -/
344	theorem chi_divisorOfList_eq_degK (L : List X.PrimeDivisor)
345	    (hbump : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
346	      chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P) :
347	    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList L) =
348	      chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k (divisorOfList L : X.WeilDivisor) := by
349	  rw [chi_telescope_list k U₀ U₁ L hbump, degK_divisorOfList]
350	
351	/-- **The Riemann inequality in closed weighted form.**  Given the closed ledger,
352	`deg_k D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)` for every `D` — the `h¹ ≥ 0` half applied to the
353	telescoped Euler characteristic.  (This is `Adelic.riemann_inequality` with its
354	`htel` hypothesis supplied from the ledger and the degree pinned to the
355	residue-weighted `deg_k`.) -/
356	theorem degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell
357	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
358	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
359	    degK k D + chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) :=
360	  riemann_inequality k U₀ U₁ (hledger D)
361	
362	end Ledger
363	
364	section LedgerNoetherian
365	
366	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
367	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
368	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
369	
370	/-- **`deg_k D < 0 ⟹ ℓ(D) = 0`** (campaign P4(a)).  Given the closed ledger: a
371	nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` would make `D` linearly equivalent to an effective divisor
372	`E = D + div f` (`exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem`); `χ` is a
373	class invariant (`chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`), so the ledger forces
374	`deg_k E = deg_k D < 0`, contradicting `deg_k E ≥ 0` for effective `E`
375	(`degK_nonneg_of_nonneg`).
376	
377	Note the shape: the hypothesis is on `deg_k`, the *weighted* degree, and the
378	argument runs entirely through the class-invariance of `χ` — no vanishing input,
379	no duality. -/
380	theorem ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg
381	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
382	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hdeg : degK k D < 0)
383	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)] :
384	    ell k D = 0 := by
385	  by_contra hne
386	  -- a nonzero section exists
387	  obtain ⟨f, hfmem, hfne⟩ : ∃ f : X.functionField, f ∈ sectionSub k ⊤ D ∧ f ≠ 0 := by
388	    by_contra hno
389	    have hbot : sectionSub k ⊤ D = ⊥ := by
390	      apply le_antisymm _ bot_le
391	      intro x hx
392	      rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
393	      · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
394	      · exact absurd ⟨x, hx, hx0⟩ hno
395	    rw [ell, hbot] at hne
396	    simp at hne
397	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEclass⟩ :=
398	    exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem hfne hfmem
399	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ hEclass
400	  rw [hledger E, hledger D] at hchi
401	  have : degK k E = degK k D := by omega
402	  have hEpos := degK_nonneg_of_nonneg k hEnonneg
403	  omega
404	
405	/-- **Principal divisors have residue-weighted degree zero** — the adelic
406	counterpart of the geometric statement `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`.
407	
408	Given the closed ledger, this is a two-line consequence of the class-invariance of
409	`χ` proved in `ClassInvariance.lean`: `0 − div g` is in the class of `0`, so
410	`χ(0 − div g) = χ(0)`, and the ledger reads off
411	`deg_k (0 − div g) = 0`, i.e. `deg_k (div g) = 0`.
412	
413	This is the *weighted* statement.  It does **not** close the open geometric leaf
414	`principal_degree_zero`, which asserts the same for the unweighted degree
415	`Σ_P ord_P g`; see §4. -/
416	theorem degK_principal_eq_zero
417	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
418	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
419	    degK k (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
420	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_principal_shift k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor) hg
421	  rw [hledger ((0 : X.WeilDivisor) - Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg),
422	    hledger (0 : X.WeilDivisor), degK_sub, degK_zero] at hchi
423	  omega
424	
425	/-- **`deg_k` descends to linear-equivalence classes.**  Given the closed ledger,
426	linearly equivalent divisors have equal weighted degree — the well-definedness
427	statement the Picard route consumes when it needs "the degree of a class". -/
428	theorem degK_eq_of_linearEquivalence
429	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
430	    {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} (h : Scheme.WeilDivisor.LinearEquivalence D D') :
431	    degK k D = degK k D' := by
432	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ h
433	  rw [hledger D, hledger D'] at hchi
434	  omega
435	
436	end LedgerNoetherian

438	section GeometricDegree

440	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

468	/-! ## §4. `degK_principal_eq_zero` versus the geometric `principal_degree_zero`
469	
470	`degK_principal_eq_zero` above and the open leaf
471	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` are **different statements**, and the
472	first does not imply the second.  Recorded here because the difference is easy to
473	misread as a formality.
474	
475	* `degK_principal_eq_zero` concerns `deg_k (div g) = Σ_P ord_P(g)·[κ(P):k]`.  Its
476	  proof is the χ-transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` plus the closed ledger, and
477	  it is stated over an **arbitrary** base field of constants `k`.
478	* `principal_degree_zero` concerns the **unweighted** `Σ_P ord_P(g)`, and is
479	  stated on a smooth proper curve over an algebraically **closed** `k̄` with no
480	  field of constants in sight and no ledger hypothesis.
481	
482	Over `k̄` the two degrees coincide because every closed point of a smooth curve has
483	residue field `k̄`, i.e. `[κ(P):k̄] = 1`.  That collapse is
484	`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, and composing it with
485	`degK_principal_eq_zero` gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`:
486	the **unweighted** statement, proved, from the ledger plus residue-degree-one.
487	
488	So the reduction is now machine-checked, and the residue of the open leaf is still two
489	items — but the first has moved to a substantially better place:
490	
491	1. `residueDeg k̄ P = 1` — **reformulated, not discharged**, in
492	   `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7.  It is proved *equivalent* to a first-order
493	   approximation statement in the order language
494	   (`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`), and that statement is then derived for
495	   an algebraically closed base from the stalk residue field
496	   (`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed`, via
497	   `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`).  **But** that derivation takes three
498	   stalk-level instance binders — `Algebra k 𝒪_P`, `IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(X)`, and
499	   `Module.Finite k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField 𝒪_P)` — none of which this project currently
500	   constructs for an AJC curve, and the last of which is effectively a new gate (it is
501	   *not* node N14's `Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)`).  So the obligation has moved
502	   from the order subquotient to standard stalk commutative algebra, which is progress, and
503	   is where it should live — but it has not gone away.  See the warning in §7 there.
504	2. The instance plumbing that places `principal_degree_zero`'s own geometric
505	   hypotheses in adelic shape: an `Algebra k̄ K(C)` with `IsConstantField k̄ C.left`
506	   (available — `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`), a 2-affine cover, **the closed ledger for
507	   that cover**, and the stalk-level `Algebra k̄ 𝒪_P` + scalar tower + residue
508	   finiteness that §7 consumes.  The ledger is the substantive one, and it is still not
509	   a theorem here (§3), so the leaf remains open.  Two of these are now sharper than
510	   before: the ledger holds on the whole *effective* cone from the one-point bump
511	   (`Adelic/LedgerClosure.lean`), and the residue input has moved from the order
512	   subquotient to the stalk (item 1 above).
513	
514	The `sorry` in `WeilDivisor.lean` is deliberately **left in place**.  Replacing it
515	with a call to `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` would require
516	producing the ledger for a cover of `C`, and the ledger is itself not yet a
517	theorem here (see §3) — so the substitution would move the gap rather than close
518	it, while making a theorem whose statement mentions no hypotheses depend silently
519	on one.  The Hartshorne II.6.10 route sketched in that docstring (build
520	`φ : C → ℙ¹` from `g`, use multiplicativity of degree under finite pullback) is a
521	*different*, heavier proof; the ledger route above is the cheaper one and is what
522	the campaign's P3 milestone anticipated. -/
523	
524	end Adelic
525	end AlgebraicGeometry

619	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective hι

621	/-! ### N14b — the residue field `κ(P)` and the residue-degree bound
622	
623	`localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` is the DVR residue field
624	`κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P`, realised as a `k`-subquotient of `K(X)`; its `k`-dimension is the
625	residue degree `deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.  For any `m`, multiplication by a rational
626	function `t` with `ord_P t = 1 - m` (which exists by `exists_order_eq` — the
627	intrinsic uniformizer-power order, *no* distinguished global uniformizer) carries
628	`orderGe P (m-1)` into `orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence
629	descends to the `k`-linear embedding `localStepTgt k P m ↪ κ(P)`.  Feeding it to
630	`localStep_finrank_le_residueEmbedding` completes node N14:
631	`dim_k (Γ(U,𝒪(D')) / Γ(U,𝒪(D))) ≤ deg P`. -/
632	
633	/-- **The residue degree `deg P := [κ(P) : k] = dim_k κ(P)`**, with the residue
634	field `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P` realised as the single-uniformizer-step valuation quotient
635	`localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1`. -/
636	noncomputable def residueDeg (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : ℕ :=
637	  Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P 1)
638	
639	/-- **The residue embedding `ι`** completing node N14.  Multiplication by a
640	rational function `t` of order `1 - m` at `P` carries `orderGe P (m-1)` into
641	`orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence descends to the
642	`k`-linear map `localStepTgt k P m → κ(P) = localStepTgt k P 1` between single-point
643	valuation quotients — the uniformizer-power shift of the fractional-ideal
644	filtration.  `k`-linearity is automatic: multiplication by a fixed element of
645	`K(X)` commutes with the `k`-action. -/
646	noncomputable def residueShift {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
647	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
648	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
649	    localStepTgt k P m →ₗ[k] localStepTgt k P 1 :=
650	  Submodule.mapQ _ _
651	    (LinearMap.restrict (LinearMap.mulLeft k t)
652	      (p := orderGeSub k P (m - 1)) (q := orderGeSub k P (1 - 1))
653	      (fun x hx => by
654	        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hx
655	        rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
656	        rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with hx0 | hx0
657	        · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
658	        · exact Or.inr (by
659	            rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]
660	            have := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx
661	            linarith)))
662	    (by
663	      intro x hx
664	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, mem_orderGeSub] at hx
665	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
666	        LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
667	      rcases eq_or_ne (x : X.functionField) 0 with hx0 | hx0
668	      · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
669	      · exact Or.inr (by
670	          rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]
671	          have := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx
672	          linarith))

674	/-- **The residue embedding is injective** (node N14, `k`-linear residue form).
675	If `t · f` lands in `orderGe P 1` then `ord_P(t·f) = (1-m) + ord_P f ≥ 1`, hence
676	`ord_P f ≥ m` and `f ∈ orderGe P m`: the kernel of the shift is exactly the tighter
677	single-point subgroup, so the induced map on the local step quotient is injective. -/
678	theorem residueShift_injective {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
679	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
680	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
681	    Function.Injective (residueShift k t ht hc) := by
682	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
683	  intro q
684	  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ q
685	  intro hq
686	  rw [residueShift, Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero,
687	    Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply,
688	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub] at hq
689	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
690	    mem_orderGeSub]
691	  rcases eq_or_ne (g : X.functionField) 0 with hg0 | hg0
692	  · rw [hg0]; exact (orderGe P m).zero_mem
693	  · refine Or.inr ?_
694	    rcases hq with h0 | h0
695	    · exact absurd ((mul_eq_zero.mp h0).resolve_left ht) hg0
696	    · rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hg0, hc] at h0
697	      linarith
698	
699	/-- **The residue embedding is surjective** (node N14, `k`-linear residue form).
700	Multiplication by the intrinsic uniformizer power `t` (order `1 - m` at `P`) is a
701	bijection of `K(X)` — inverse multiplication by `t⁻¹` — carrying `orderGe P (m-1)`
702	*onto* `orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` onto `orderGe P 1`.  Hence the descended map
703	`residueShift` is surjective: an isomorphism
704	`orderGe P (m-1)/orderGe P m ≅ κ(P) = orderGe P 0/orderGe P 1`. -/
705	theorem residueShift_surjective {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
706	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
707	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
708	    Function.Surjective (residueShift k t ht hc) := by
709	  intro z
710	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
711	  have hmem : t⁻¹ * (y : X.functionField) ∈ orderGe P (m - 1) := by
712	    rcases eq_or_ne (y : X.functionField) 0 with hy0 | hy0
713	    · rw [hy0, mul_zero]; exact (orderGe P (m - 1)).zero_mem
714	    · refine (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (inv_ne_zero ht) hy0)).mpr ?_
715	      have hy : (1 - 1 : ℤ) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (y : X.functionField) :=
716	        (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hy0).mp y.2
717	      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P (inv_ne_zero ht) hy0,
718	        Scheme.RationalMap.order_inv, hc]
719	      linarith
720	  refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨t⁻¹ * (y : X.functionField),
721	    (mem_orderGeSub k).mpr hmem⟩, ?_⟩
722	  rw [residueShift, Submodule.mapQ_apply]
723	  congr 1
724	  apply Subtype.ext
725	  rw [LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
726	  exact mul_inv_cancel_left₀ ht _

728	/-- **The single-point valuation quotient has dimension `deg P` for every shift.**
729	Multiplication by an intrinsic uniformizer power intertwines the steps of the
730	fractional-ideal filtration, so every one-step valuation quotient
731	`orderGe P (m-1)/orderGe P m` is `k`-isomorphic to the residue field
732	`κ(P) = orderGe P 0/orderGe P 1`; hence they all share the residue degree
733	`deg P = [κ(P):k]`.  (`residueShift` is a bijection: injective by
734	`residueShift_injective`, surjective by `residueShift_surjective`.) -/
735	theorem finrank_localStepTgt (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) :
736	    Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P m) = residueDeg k P := by
737	  obtain ⟨t, ht, htord⟩ := exists_order_eq P (1 - m)
738	  rw [residueDeg]
739	  exact (LinearEquiv.ofBijective (residueShift k t ht htord)
740	    ⟨residueShift_injective k t ht htord, residueShift_surjective k t ht htord⟩).finrank_eq
741	
742	/-- **N14 — the local step dimension is at most the residue degree.**  For the
743	one-point twist `D' = D + P` (with `P ∈ U`, `D'(P) = D(P) + 1`, `D = D'` off `P`)
744	the local step space `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) / Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` has `k`-dimension at most the
745	residue degree `deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.  This is the honest conclusion of N14: the
746	composite of the elementary kernel injection (`localStepMapₖ_injective`) with the
747	uniformizer-power residue embedding (`residueShift_injective`).  The finiteness of
748	`κ(P)` over `k` — `[κ(P):k] < ∞`, the residue field of a closed point of a
749	finite-type `k`-curve — is the gated keystone input `[Module.Finite k κ(P)]`, not
750	re-proved here. -/
751	theorem localStep_finrank_le {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
752	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
753	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
754	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
755	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
756	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
757	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
758	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
759	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
760	    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k U D D') ≤ residueDeg k P := by
761	  obtain ⟨t, ht, htord⟩ :=
762	    exists_order_eq P (1 - (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P))
763	  exact localStep_finrank_le_residueEmbedding k hPU hstep hle hoff
764	    (residueShift k t ht htord) (residueShift_injective k t ht htord)
765	
766	/-! ### N14 (equality direction) — the residue map is onto: strong approximation
767	
768	The `≤` bound above is the elementary half.  The reverse — that the local step space
769	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D))` fills *all* of the residue field `κ(P)` — is the surjectivity
770	of the local residue map, i.e. the **strong/weak-approximation** input: any prescribed
771	residue at `P` (any `y` with `ord_P y ≥ -n-1`) is realised, to residue precision at
772	`P` (modulo `orderGe P (-n)`), by a global-on-`U` section of `𝒪(D')`.  We take this
773	existence as the honest hypothesis `hsurj` (discharged at the use site from the
774	Dedekind-chart CRT / weak approximation for the finitely many constraint places), and
775	from it obtain the local isomorphism and the exact dimension count `= deg P`. -/
776	
777	/-- **N14 (equality direction) — the `k`-linear local step map is surjective.**  Given
778	the strong-approximation existence hypothesis `hsurj` — every rational function of
779	order `≥ -n-1` at `P` is matched, modulo `orderGe P (-n)` (to residue precision at
780	`P`), by a section of `𝒪(D')` on `U` — the residue map
781	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D)) → orderGe P (-n-1)/orderGe P (-n)` is onto. -/
782	theorem localStepMapₖ_surjective {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
783	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
784	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
785	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
786	    (hsurj : ∀ y : X.functionField,
787	        y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) →
788	        ∃ f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D',
789	          f - y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)) :
790	    Function.Surjective (localStepMapₖ k hPU hstep) := by
791	  intro z
792	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
793	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfy⟩ := hsurj (y : X.functionField) ((mem_orderGeSub k).mp y.2)
794	  refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨f, (mem_sectionSub k).mpr hf⟩, ?_⟩
795	  rw [localStepMapₖ, Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
796	    Submodule.subtype_apply, AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub, Submodule.coe_inclusion,
797	    mem_orderGeSub]
798	  exact hfy
799	
800	/-- **N14 (equality direction) — the local step has dimension exactly `deg P`.**  Under
801	the strong-approximation surjectivity `hsurj`, the `k`-linear local step map
802	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D)) → orderGe P (-n-1)/orderGe P (-n)` is bijective (injective by
803	`localStepMapₖ_injective`, surjective by `localStepMapₖ_surjective`), so the local step
804	space is `k`-isomorphic to the single-point valuation quotient, whose dimension is the
805	residue degree (`finrank_localStepTgt`):
806	`dim_k(Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D))) = deg P = [κ(P):k]`.  This is the exact one-point count
807	underlying `χ(D+P) = χ(D) + deg P`; no finiteness gate is needed (a linear equivalence,
808	whose `finrank` equality is unconditional). -/
809	theorem localStep_finrank_eq {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
810	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
811	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
812	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
813	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
814	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
815	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
816	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
817	    (hsurj : ∀ y : X.functionField,
818	        y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) →
819	        ∃ f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D',
820	          f - y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)) :
821	    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k U D D') = residueDeg k P := by
822	  rw [(LinearEquiv.ofBijective (localStepMapₖ k hPU hstep)
823	      ⟨localStepMapₖ_injective k hPU hstep hle hoff,
824	        localStepMapₖ_surjective k hPU hstep hsurj⟩).finrank_eq,

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — closing the ledger from the one-point bump
10	
11	Every conditional statement of the vanishing and generation lane
12	(`Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` §3, `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`,
13	`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`) takes the **closed ledger**
14	
15	`hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`
16	
17	as a hypothesis quantified over **all** Weil divisors.  `chi_telescope_list` establishes
18	it for *effective* divisors from the one-point bump, and the sibling docstrings record
19	that "extending from list-effective divisors to all divisors additionally needs the
20	negative part" as an open item.
21	
22	This file settles **half** of that extension and states the other half exactly.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	`chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg` — the ledger holds at **every effective divisor**, from the
27	one-point bump alone, with the list eliminated from the statement.  This is a real
28	strengthening of `chi_telescope_list`: every effective divisor is list-effective
29	(`exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg`), so a consumer no longer has to produce a list.
30	
31	## What is *not* proved, stated precisely
32	
33	`chi_eq_iff_step_of_bump` — given the bump, the ledger at an arbitrary `D` is
34	**equivalent** to the single identity `χ(D⁺) − χ(D) = deg_k (−D)⁺`.  It is deliberately an
35	`iff` and not a one-directional "reduction": the two sides are interderivable by
36	arithmetic, so a `←`-only version would be a theorem that re-indexes its own conclusion.
37	That failure mode is exactly what inbox memory I-0399 records for this task, and the
38	`iff` is how this file avoids repeating it.
39	
40	## Why the naive route fails
41	
42	The lattice identity `D + (−D)⁺ = D⁺` — pointwise `n + max(−n,0) = max(n,0)` — writes any
43	divisor as a difference of two effective ones, and the effective case above handles both
44	pieces.  But that does not close the ledger, because the two transport mechanisms the lane
45	owns do not apply:
46	
47	* `χ` is **not additive** in the divisor.  Only `deg_k` is (`degKHom`), which is why the
48	  arithmetic above goes through on the degree side and stops on the `χ` side.
49	* `D` and `D⁺` are **not linearly equivalent** in general, so the class-invariance
50	  transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` cannot move `χ` between them.
51	
52	So the negative part is not bookkeeping that a more careful induction would absorb; it
53	needs an input the project does not have.  Recorded here rather than left implicit, because
54	the sibling docstrings describe it as merely "additionally needs the negative part", which
55	understates it.
56	-/

133

135	
136	`χ(D⁺) − χ(D) = deg_k (−D)⁺`,
137	
138	i.e. to "`χ` drops by the weighted degree of the removed negative part".  Both directions
139	are proved, so this is *not* a theorem that reduces the ledger to something cheaper — it is
140	a statement of exactly what the remaining content is.

143	"bump + hstep ⟹ ledger at `D`", and present it as progress.  That would be misleading in
144	the specific way I-0399 records for this task: given `hbump` (which pins the ledger at

161	  have hpos := chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg k U₀ U₁ hbump (positivePart_nonneg D)

164	    rw [← degK_sub, ← eq_positivePart_sub_negativePart D]

166	  · intro h; omega

956	    (connect : localStepDom k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D D' →ₗ[k] H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)

809	  have hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField) :=
810	    IsFractionRing.injective _ _
811	  have hbne : (b : Γ(X, U)) ≠ 0 := nonZeroDivisors.ne_zero b.2
812	  have halgb : algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField (b : Γ(X, U)) ≠ 0 := fun h =>
813	    hbne (hinj (by rw [h, map_zero]))

816	  have halga : algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField a ≠ 0 := fun h =>
817	    hane (hinj (by rw [h, map_zero]))

819	      (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField (b : Γ(X, U)))⁻¹ := by
820	    rw [← hab, mul_inv_cancel_right₀ halgb]
821	  -- the finite bounding set of primes
822	  have hBfin :
823	      ({q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, U) | q.asIdeal ∈ (Ideal.span {a}).minimalPrimes} ∪
824	        {q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, U) |
825	          q.asIdeal ∈ (Ideal.span {(b : Γ(X, U))}).minimalPrimes}).Finite := by
826	    refine Set.Finite.union ?_ ?_
827	    · exact (Ideal.finite_minimalPrimes_of_isNoetherianRing Γ(X, U)
828	        (Ideal.span {a})).preimage (Set.injOn_of_injective (fun _ _ h => PrimeSpectrum.ext h))
829	    · exact (Ideal.finite_minimalPrimes_of_isNoetherianRing Γ(X, U)
830	        (Ideal.span {(b : Γ(X, U))})).preimage
831	        (Set.injOn_of_injective (fun _ _ h => PrimeSpectrum.ext h))
832	  -- total map with junk value into PrimeSpectrum
833	  let junk : PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, U) := ⟨⊥, Ideal.isPrime_bot⟩
834	  let Φ : X.PrimeDivisor → PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, U) :=
835	    fun Y => if h : Y.point ∈ U then hU.primeIdealOf ⟨Y.point, h⟩ else junk
836	  apply Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := Φ)
837	  · refine hBfin.subset ?_
838	    rintro q ⟨Y, ⟨hYU, hord⟩, rfl⟩
839	    simp only [Φ, dif_pos hYU]
840	    have hheight := primeIdealOf_height_eq_one hU Y hYU
841	    haveI : (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨Y.point, hYU⟩).asIdeal.IsPrime :=
842	      (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨Y.point, hYU⟩).isPrime
843	    have hmem : a ∈ (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨Y.point, hYU⟩).asIdeal ∨
844	        (b : Γ(X, U)) ∈ (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨Y.point, hYU⟩).asIdeal := by
845	      by_contra hcon
846	      rw [not_or] at hcon
847	      apply hord
848	      rw [hfeq,
849	        Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero Y halga (inv_ne_zero halgb),
850	        Scheme.RationalMap.order_inv,
851	        order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_notMem_primeIdealOf hU Y hYU a hcon.1,
852	        order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_notMem_primeIdealOf hU Y hYU (b : Γ(X, U)) hcon.2]
853	      ring
854	    rcases hmem with hmem | hmem
855	    · exact Or.inl (mem_minimalPrimes_of_height_one hheight hane hmem)
856	    · exact Or.inr (mem_minimalPrimes_of_height_one hheight hbne hmem)
857	  · rintro Y ⟨hYU, -⟩ Y' ⟨hY'U, -⟩ hΦ
858	    simp only [Φ, dif_pos hYU, dif_pos hY'U] at hΦ
859	    have := congrArg hU.fromSpec hΦ
860	    rw [hU.fromSpec_primeIdealOf, hU.fromSpec_primeIdealOf] at this
861	    exact Scheme.PrimeDivisor.ext this
862	
863	end FiniteSupport
864	
865	/-- **Hartshorne II.6.1**: for a nonzero rational function `f` on a Noetherian
866	integral scheme `X` satisfying `(*)`, the order function `Y ↦ ord_Y(f)` is
867	nonzero at only finitely many prime divisors `Y`. This is the well-definedness
868	side condition for `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal`.
869	
870	The proof uses a finite affine cover and the fact that only finitely many
871	height-one primes can divide the numerator or denominator on each chart.
872	
873	The statement is generic in `f` (no `f ≠ 0` hypothesis is threaded): on
874	`f = 0` the function `Y ↦ ord_Y(0) = WithZero.log 0 = 0` has empty support,
875	which is finite, so the conclusion holds vacuously. -/
876	theorem rationalMap_order_finite_support {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
877	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
878	    (f : X.functionField) :
879	    (Function.support (fun Y : X.PrimeDivisor =>
880	      Scheme.RationalMap.order Y f)).Finite := by
881	  -- Case 1 (f = 0): the order function evaluates to
882	  -- `WithZero.log (Ring.ordFrac _ 0) = WithZero.log 0 = 0` at every
883	  -- prime divisor, so the support is empty (finite vacuously).
884	  by_cases hf : f = 0
885	  · subst hf
886	    convert Set.finite_empty
887	    ext Y
888	    simp only [Function.mem_support, ne_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false,
889	      Decidable.not_not, Scheme.RationalMap.order_zero]
890	  -- Case 2 (f ≠ 0): Stacks 02RV. Global Noetherian = quasi-compact gives a
891	  -- FINITE affine cover `X = ⋃ᵢ Uᵢ`; every prime divisor's generic point lies in
892	  -- some `Uᵢ`, so the support is contained in the finite union of the per-chart
893	  -- supports, each finite by `finite_chart_support` (the affine-chart
894	  -- minimal-primes core).  Without `[CompactSpace X]` (equivalently
895	  -- `[IsNoetherian X]`) this fails: the line with infinitely many origins is a
896	  -- non-quasi-compact counterexample.
897	  · haveI : CompactSpace X := inferInstance
898	    set 𝒰 := X.affineCover.finiteSubcover with h𝒰
899	    refine Set.Finite.subset (Set.finite_iUnion fun i : 𝒰.I₀ =>
900	      finite_chart_support (isAffineOpen_opensRange (𝒰.f i)) hf) ?_
901	    intro Y hY
902	    refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨𝒰.idx Y.point, ?_, hY⟩
903	    exact 𝒰.covers Y.point

2	name: lean-check
3	description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
4	---
5	
6	## Required proof loop
7	
8	Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
9	at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
10	`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
11	before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
12	search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.
13	
14	Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
15	check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
16	validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
17	unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
18	usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
19	the check.
20	
21	LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
22	module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
23	configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
24	the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
25	only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
26	specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.
27	
28	- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
29	  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
30	  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
31	- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
32	  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
33	  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
34	  project root.
35	- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
36	  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
37	- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
38	- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
39	  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
40	- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
41	  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.
42	
43	## Fast LSP proving loop
44	
45	The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
46	(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:
47	
48	- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
49	  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
50	- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
51	  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
52	- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
53	  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
54	  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
55	- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
56	  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
57	  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
58	  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.
59	
60	Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
61	skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
62	candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
63	kernel-check the module at the end.
64	
65	## Heavy builds — actually wait for them
66	
67	Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
68	deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
69	ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
70	or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
71	"Warnings are work").
72	
73	A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
74	most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
75	build to finish**:
76	
77	- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
78	  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
79	  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
80	  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
81	- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
82	  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
83	  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
84	  is *not* done.
85	- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
86	  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
87	  for final validation.
88	- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
89	  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
90	  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
91	  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
92	- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
93	  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
94	  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
95	  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.
96	
97	## When the LSP dies on big import files
98	
99	The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
100	imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
101	that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
102	run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
103	proof error:
104	
105	- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
106	  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
107	  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
108	- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
109	  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
110	  the specific module you are proving in instead.
111	- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
112	  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

403	/-- **Order-nonnegativity is stalk-integrality.** For a nonzero rational function
404	`f`, `ord_P f ≥ 0` exactly when `f` lifts to the DVR stalk `𝒪_P = 𝒪_{X,P}`, i.e.
405	`f = a` for some `a ∈ 𝒪_P` (viewed in `K` via the fraction-field embedding). This
406	is the additive-normalisation reading of `v_P(f) ≤ 1 ⟺ f ∈ 𝒪_P`. -/
407	theorem exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
408	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0)
409	    (hord : 0 ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) :
410	    ∃ a : X.presheaf.stalk P.point,
411	      algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk P.point) X.functionField a = f := by
412	  have hpv : pointValuation P f ≠ 0 := by
413	    simpa using (Valuation.zero_iff (pointValuation P)).not.mpr hf
414	  have hlog : WithZero.log (pointValuation P f) ≤ 0 := by
415	    have := order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation P f
416	    rw [this] at hord; linarith
417	  have hle1 : pointValuation P f ≤ 1 := by
418	    have : WithZero.log (pointValuation P f) ≤ WithZero.log (1 : ℤᵐ⁰) := by
419	      simpa using hlog
420	    exact (WithZero.log_le_log hpv one_ne_zero).mp this
421	  exact IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_lift_of_le_one hle1
422	
423	/-- **Order surjectivity: every integer is realised as an order at `P`.**  The DVR
424	stalk `𝒪_P` has a uniformizer `π` with `ord_P π = 1` — the maximal-ideal
425	height-one place, whose adic valuation is `exp (-1)` (mathlib's
426	`IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_exists_uniformizer`) — and its integer
427	powers `π^j` realise every order `j : ℤ`.  This is the surjectivity of
428	`ord_P : K(X) → ℤ`; only the intrinsic order value of the DVR uniformizer is used,
429	never a distinguished *global* uniformizer (a fixed rational function). -/
430	theorem exists_order_eq (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (j : ℤ) :
431	    ∃ t : X.functionField, t ≠ 0 ∧ Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = j := by
432	  obtain ⟨π, hπ⟩ :=

10	/-!
11	# Discharge of the adelic `IsConstantField` gate (campaign P-cluster opener)
12	
13	The χ-ledger of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiLedger.lean` runs over a base field of
14	constants `k ↪ K(X)` packaged by the gate class `Adelic.IsConstantField k X`:
15	*every nonzero constant has order `0` at every prime divisor*.  The W1-F audit
16	dossier (run 0020) flagged this gate as instance-free and absent from the
17	campaign gate table.  This file discharges it for the situation the campaign
18	actually uses: a curve `C : Over (Spec k)` with the `k`-algebra structure on the
19	function field induced by the structure morphism.
20	
21	## Statement audit (BLOCKING house rule; verdict recorded before proving)
22	
23	* The gate `IsConstantField k X` asserts only the **easy direction** of the
24	  field-of-constants dialectic: nonzero constants are everywhere units, i.e.
25	  `ord_P (c) = 0` for `c ∈ k^×`.  With the algebra structure factoring through
26	  `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → 𝒪_{C,P} → K(C)`, this is TRUE at full generality: a nonzero
27	  `c` is a unit in the field `k`, ring maps preserve units, so its image in the
28	  DVR stalk `𝒪_{C,P}` is a unit, and `Ring.ordFrac` of a stalk unit is `1`
29	  (Mathlib `Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit`), i.e. `ord_P = 0`.  **No properness, no
30	  geometric integrality, no `B0` input is needed** — only `[IsIntegral C.left]`
31	  (for the function-field formalism) plus the standing `(*)`-hypotheses
32	  `[IsLocallyNoetherian]`, `[IsRegularInCodimensionOne]` of the `order` API.
33	* The W1-F dossier proposed discharging the gate "via B0's
34	  `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`".  Correction (this file): `B0`/
35	  `HasTrivialConstants` is the content of the **converse** direction — that
36	  every everywhere-regular function is a constant, `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` — which the
37	  gate does *not* assert.  `B0` enters only as the natural home of the ring map
38	  `constMap C : k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` used to *define* the algebra structure
39	  (`functionFieldAlgebra` below); that map exists for every `C : Over (Spec k)`.
40	* Instance-diamond audit: Mathlib has **no** `Algebra k X.functionField`
41	  instance for a plain field `k` (only `Algebra Γ(X, U) X.functionField` and
42	  `Algebra (𝒪_{X,x}) X.functionField`), so `functionFieldAlgebra` creates no
43	  diamond.  It is `scoped` (house pattern of
44	  `Scheme.globalSectionsAlgebra`, `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`) — the
45	  χ-ledger consumer opens `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` to activate it together
46	  with the gate instance.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit` — reusable brick: the
51	  order of (the image in `K(X)` of) a stalk unit at a prime divisor is `0`.
52	* `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `K(C)` induced by
53	  the structure morphism, through `constMap` and the germ at the generic point.
54	* `Scheme.instIsConstantField` — the gate discharge.
55	
56	Campaign reference: wave-2 P-cluster opener (task A) of
57	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`; W1-F dossier §7 gate inventory.

59	
60	universe u
61	
62	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
65	
66	/-- **Order of a stalk unit is zero.**  For a prime divisor `Y` of a scheme `X`
67	satisfying the standing `(*)`-hypotheses, and a *unit* `u` of the DVR stalk
68	`𝒪_{X,Y}`, the order of vanishing of its image in the function field is `0`:
69	units have neither zeros nor poles along `Y`.  Wrapper around Mathlib's
70	`Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit` through the definition
71	`order Y f = WithZero.log (Ring.ordFrac 𝒪_{X,Y} f)`. -/
72	theorem Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit
73	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
74	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] (Y : X.PrimeDivisor)
75	    {u : X.presheaf.stalk Y.point} (hu : IsUnit u) :
76	    Scheme.RationalMap.order Y
77	      (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk Y.point) X.functionField u) = 0 := by
78	  unfold Scheme.RationalMap.order
79	  rw [Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit hu, WithZero.log_one]
80	
81	namespace Scheme
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
84	
85	/-- The total open `⊤` of an irreducible (e.g. integral) scheme is nonempty —
86	instance form, so that instance heads mentioning the Mathlib
87	`Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) X.functionField` (which carries a `[Nonempty ⊤]` binder) can
88	synthesize.  Scoped to avoid polluting general `Nonempty` searches. -/
89	scoped instance nonempty_top_opens (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X] :
90	    Nonempty (⊤ : X.Opens) :=
91	  ⟨⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩⟩
92	
93	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on the function field `K(C)` of an integral
94	`k`-scheme `C`, induced by the structure morphism: the composite
95	`k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → K(C)` of `constMap C` (`Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`)
96	with the germ at the generic point.  Scoped, mirroring
97	`globalSectionsAlgebra`. -/
98	noncomputable scoped instance functionFieldAlgebra
99	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left] :
100	    Algebra k C.left.functionField :=
101	  RingHom.toAlgebra ((C.left.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.comp (constMap C).hom)
102	
103	/-- The `k`-algebra map to the function field factors through the global
104	sections: `algebraMap k K(C) = germToFunctionField ∘ constMap` — definitional
105	unfolding of `functionFieldAlgebra`, stated against the Mathlib
106	`Algebra Γ(C, ⊤) K(C)` instance. -/
107	lemma algebraMap_functionField_eq (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
108	    [IsIntegral C.left] :
109	    algebraMap k C.left.functionField
110	      = (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField).comp (constMap C).hom :=
111	  rfl
112	
113	/-- The tower `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → K(C)` of the structure-morphism algebra
114	structures. -/
115	scoped instance isScalarTower_globalSections_functionField
116	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left] :
117	    IsScalarTower k ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField :=
118	  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_functionField_eq C)
119	
120	/-- **The structure field satisfies the adelic `IsConstantField` interface.**
121	For an integral
122	`k`-scheme `C` satisfying the `(*)`-hypotheses, with the structure-morphism
123	algebra structure on `K(C)`, every nonzero constant `c ∈ k` has order `0` at
124	every prime divisor: `c` is a unit in the field `k`, hence its image in each
125	DVR stalk is a unit, and units have order `0`
126	(`order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit`).
127	
128	Audit verdict (see module docstring): TRUE at this generality — no properness,
129	no `B0`/`HasTrivialConstants` input; this is the easy direction of the
130	field-of-constants dialectic. -/
131	theorem isConstantField_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
132	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
133	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
134	    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left where
135	  order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc := by
136	    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) :=
137	      C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk
138	        (⟨P.point, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
139	    haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
140	        C.left.functionField :=
141	      functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨P.point, trivial⟩
142	    have h1 : algebraMap k C.left.functionField c
143	        = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField ((constMap C).hom c) := rfl
144	    have hu : IsUnit (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
145	        ((constMap C).hom c)) :=
146	      ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hc).map (constMap C).hom).map _
147	    rw [h1, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)
148	      (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) C.left.functionField]
149	    exact Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit P hu
150	
151	/-- Scoped instance form of `isConstantField_functionField`. -/
152	scoped instance instIsConstantField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
153	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
154	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
155	    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left :=
156	  isConstantField_functionField C
157	
158	end Scheme
159	
160	end AlgebraicGeometry

11	/-!
12	# Schemes over algebraically closed fields
13	
14	We show that if `X` is locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field `k`,
15	then the closed points of `X` are in bijection with the `k`-points of `X`.
16	See `AlgebraicGeometry.pointEquivClosedPoint`.

28	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
29	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed {x})

31	/-- If `X` is a locally of finite type `k`-scheme and `k` is algebraically closed, then
32	the residue field of any closed point of `x` is isomorphic to `k`. -/

34	  letI : IsIso (Spec.preimage (X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ f)) := by
35	    have : IsFinite (X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ f) := by
36	      rw [isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion] at hx
37	      rw [isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace]
38	      infer_instance

40	    refine IsAlgClosed.ringHom_bijective_of_isIntegral _ ?_

47	    Spec.map (residueFieldIsoBase f x hx).inv = X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ f :=
48	  Spec.map_preimage _

53	  Spec.map (residueFieldIsoBase f x hx).hom ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x

70	    have := isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id _ _ p.2
71	    have := p.1.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
72	    rwa [Set.range_eq_singleton] at this
73	    exact fun x ↦ congr(p.1 $(Subsingleton.elim _ _))⟩
74	  invFun x := ⟨pointOfClosedPoint f x.1 x.2, pointOfClosedPoint_comp f x.1 x.2⟩
75	  left_inv p := by
76	    ext
77	    refine ((Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField _ _).symm_apply_eq (x := ⟨_, _⟩)).mpr ?_
78	    rw [Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField_eq_iff]
79	    dsimp [Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField]

81	    generalize_proofs _ h
82	    refine (Category.comp_id _).symm.trans (((residueFieldIsoBase f _ h).eq_inv_comp).mp ?_)
83	    rw [← Spec.map_injective.eq_iff]

85	    rw [reassoc_of% Scheme.descResidueField_stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecResidueField, p.2]

89	    {f g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X} (h : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
90	    [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
91	    (hf : f ≫ h = 𝟙 _) (hg : g ≫ h = 𝟙 _)

99	    [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ i)]

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ClosedPoint

/-!
# Finiteness and positivity of the residue degree at a closed point

For a scheme `X` smooth of relative dimension one over a field `K`, integral, and locally of
finite type (the curve bundle of the Jacobian challenge), the residue field `κ(x)` at a
non-generic (hence closed) point `x` is a *finite* extension of `K`, and its degree is
positive:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.residueDeg_finite`: `κ(x)` is a finite `K`-module;
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.residueDeg_pos`: `0 < [κ(x) : K]`.

The `K`-module structure on `κ(x)` is the landed `Scheme.residueFieldOverModule K X x` (restriction
of scalars along the explicit ring hom `Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap`), activated as a local
instance below.

## Mathematical route (Zariski's lemma through a chart)

A closed point `x` lies in a Dedekind affine chart `V ∋ x` with section ring `B := Γ(X, V)`; the
prime `q := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, _⟩` is nonzero, hence maximal, so `B ⧸ q` is a field. Two facts
combine:

1. **Finite type ⇒ finite (Zariski/Jacobson).** `K → B` is of finite type (locally of finite type
   applied to the chart), so `K → B → B ⧸ q` is a finite-type map into a *field*; over the
   Jacobson ring `K`, `finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing` upgrades finite type to finite.
2. **`κ(x) ≅ B ⧸ q` `K`-linearly.** The stalk `𝒪_{X,x}` is the localization of `B` at `q`, so its
   residue field is `q.ResidueField`; for maximal `q` this is `B ⧸ q`. Transporting the module
   finiteness along this ring iso — shown `K`-linear by a compatibility of structure maps through
   the chart — gives finiteness of `κ(x)`.

Positivity is then `Module.finrank_pos_iff_of_free` for the nontrivial free finite module `κ(x)`
over the field `K`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.residueFieldOverModule

/-- A nonzero-prime witness at a closed point of an affine Dedekind chart: on an integral scheme
with a domain section ring, the prime of `Γ(X, V)` cut out by a non-generic point of an affine open
is not `⊥`. (Re-derivation of the ne-bot fact used in `IsAffineOpen.isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk`.)
-/
private theorem primeIdealOf_ne_bot {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] {V : X.Opens}
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) [IsDomain Γ(X, V)] {x : X} (hx : x ∈ V) (hxg : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
    (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal ≠ ⊥ := by
  intro h
  apply hxg
  have h1 : hV.fromSpec.base (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩) = x := hV.fromSpec_primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hgen : (genericPoint (Spec Γ(X, V)) : Spec Γ(X, V)) = hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ := by
    rw [genericPoint_eq_bot_of_affine]
    exact (PrimeSpectrum.ext h).symm
  rw [← h1, ← hgen, genericPoint_eq_of_isOpenImmersion hV.fromSpec]

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- **Finiteness of the residue degree at a closed point.** On an integral scheme smooth of
relative dimension one and locally of finite type over a field `K`, the residue field at a
non-generic point is a finite `K`-module. -/
theorem Scheme.residueDeg_finite
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
    Module.Finite K (X.residueField x) := by
  -- A Dedekind affine chart `V ∋ x`, its section ring `Γ(X, V)`, and the nonzero maximal prime `q`.
  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hD⟩ :=
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) x
  haveI := hD
  letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) (X.presheaf.stalk x) := X.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk ⟨x, hxV⟩
  haveI hloc : IsLocalization.AtPrime (X.presheaf.stalk x) (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxV⟩).asIdeal :=
    hV.isLocalization_stalk ⟨x, hxV⟩
  set q := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxV⟩ with hq
  haveI : q.asIdeal.IsPrime := q.isPrime
  haveI hmax : q.asIdeal.IsMaximal := q.isPrime.isMaximal (primeIdealOf_ne_bot hV hxV hx)
  letI : Field (Γ(X, V) ⧸ q.asIdeal) := Ideal.Quotient.field q.asIdeal
  -- The residue-field ring iso `B ⧸ q ≃+* κ(x)`, from the localization and the maximal quotient.
  set φ' := IsLocalization.algEquiv q.asIdeal.primeCompl (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
    (X.presheaf.stalk x) with hφ'
  set m := IsLocalRing.ResidueField.mapEquiv φ'.toRingEquiv with hm
  set b := RingEquiv.ofBijective (algebraMap (Γ(X, V) ⧸ q.asIdeal) q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
    (Ideal.bijective_algebraMap_quotient_residueField q.asIdeal) with hb
  set e' := b.trans m with he'
  -- The finite-type structure map `ψ : K → B ⧸ q`.
  set ψ := (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal).comp (X.overAlgebraMap K V) with hψ
  -- `κ(x)` seen through the chart: `residue ∘ germ_V ∘ overAlgebraMap_V`.
  have hmid : (X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom.comp (X.overAlgebraMap K ⊤)
      = (X.presheaf.germ V x hxV).hom.comp (X.overAlgebraMap K V) := by
    have hgr : X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial
        = X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op ≫ X.presheaf.germ V x hxV :=
      (X.presheaf.germ_res (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)) x hxV).symm
    rw [hgr, CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_assoc,
      X.overAlgebraMap_naturality K (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op]
  have hchart : X.residueOverAlgebraMap K x
      = ((X.residue x).hom.comp (X.presheaf.germ V x hxV).hom).comp (X.overAlgebraMap K V) := by
    rw [Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap, hmid, ← RingHom.comp_assoc]
  -- Core compatibility of the ring iso with the chart's residue map (no `K` involved).
  have hcore : e'.toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal)
      = (X.residue x).hom.comp (X.presheaf.germ V x hxV).hom := by
    ext y
    simp only [he', hb, hm, RingHom.comp_apply, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe,
      RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.trans_apply, RingEquiv.coe_ofBijective,
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.mapEquiv_apply, Ideal.algebraMap_quotient_residueField_mk]
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply Γ(X, V) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        q.asIdeal.ResidueField, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq,
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map_residue]
    simp only [RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv, AlgEquiv.commutes]
    rfl
  -- `K`-linear compatibility `e' (ψ c) = residueOverAlgebraMap c`.
  have hcompat : ∀ c : K, e' (ψ c) = X.residueOverAlgebraMap K x c := fun c => by
    have h := DFunLike.congr_fun hcore (X.overAlgebraMap K V c)
    rw [hchart]
    exact h
  -- Finiteness of `B ⧸ q` over `K` by Zariski's lemma (finite type into a field, Jacobson base).
  letI : Algebra K (Γ(X, V) ⧸ q.asIdeal) := ψ.toAlgebra
  have hoa : (X.overAlgebraMap K V).FiniteType := by
    have happ : X.overAlgebraMap K V = ((X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).appLE ⊤ V le_top).hom.comp
        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom := by
      rw [Scheme.overAlgebraMap, CommRingCat.hom_comp]; rfl
    rw [happ]
    exact RingHom.FiniteType.comp
      ((X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).finiteType_appLE (isAffineOpen_top _) hV le_top)
      (RingHom.FiniteType.of_surjective _
        (((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
          (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv).mp inferInstance).surjective))
  have hψft : ψ.FiniteType := by
    rw [hψ]; exact RingHom.FiniteType.comp_surjective hoa Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
  haveI : Algebra.FiniteType K (Γ(X, V) ⧸ q.asIdeal) := hψft
